items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: I grew up playing with Steve Kuhn and Arnie Wise

ctx.x: Was part of it trying to find your way in the culture of it? Not just the playing but the nightlife and the language and the camaraderie.

Absolutely. And I had to do that in my own personal way. White, middle class Jewish kid from an educated family, hanging out with other quite smart people but whose smarts were oriented in slightly different ways from mine and some of whom were drinking and smoking pot and I wasn’t ready for any of that. So I had to figure out how to be in it and a part of it without, well I had to find a way to fit in. And interestingly it was a pretty wide open society of people that would accept me being there, even though I…

I’m not going to spend a lot of time on this but you, in a fairly recent interview which I thought was done very well from a fellow out there, you spoke about being in a hotel room with Bill Evans and watching him basically shoot up and I’m wondering why the drinking and the drugs has been associated with jazz. I’m sure it’s overblown but you are saying it was part of the scene. Do you know why?
